findings.title: [P1] Validate output-derived paths before opening them on the host
findings.body: Container output controls `f` without path validation. A malicious submission can emit `ERROR /dev/zero` followed by `1 error in 0.01s`; the host then executes `open('/dev/zero').read()`, consuming memory indefinitely outside the container timeout. Absolute paths, traversal paths and escaping symlinks also permit reads outside the grading tree. Apply containment checks to both this read and `def_line`, require regular files, and bound reads.

findings.failure_mode: Container output controls `f` without path validation.

findings.title: [P1] Reject failed executions before accepting claimed test results
findings.body: When output parses, `run_suite` preserves claimed passes regardless of the exit status, and `all_pass` ignores both `rc` and `timed_out`. Submission-controlled code can emit a fabricated summary such as `1000000 passed in 0.01s` and terminate before running hidden tests. The parser requires no corresponding outcome records, so this produces full credit and can mark an APPROVED verdict accurate. Require successful execution and validate claimed results against expected test cases before accepting a pass.

findings.failure_mode: When output parses, `run_suite` preserves claimed passes regardless of the exit status, and `all_pass` ignores both `rc` and `timed_out`.

findings.description: Hidden-test results are derived solely from parsing the stdout of a process that executes agent-controlled code. The hidden tests are overlaid onto the agent's tree and import the agent's modules; the agent's conftest.py / pytest.ini (addopts) / any imported module runs in the same pytest process (container mode even passes -s, so prints go straight to the captured stream). A module can print `PASSED tests/test_x.py::t` lines plus a fake `===== 12 passed in 0.1s =====` summary and call os._exit(0); parse_pytest takes the last matching summary, all_pass() is true and hidden_tests/snapshot_tests/verdict_accuracy are forged. Separately, run_suite (line 631-633) sets passed=total whenever no summary parses and rc==0, so a conftest that os._exit(0)s at import yields a full-score passed/total (only parse_error distinguishes it, and downstream consumers may not check it).
findings.failure_mode: The graded agent (or any code it leaves in sandbox/) fabricates a perfect hidden-test, regression and structural grade; the ablation results are untrustworthy.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not trust the terminal output. Load a grader-owned pytest plugin via `-p` (mounted read-only from a path outside /workspace) that writes machine-readable results to a second mount (`-v <scratch>:/results`) and cross-check: number of collected hidden node ids must equal the ids statically enumerated from the overlaid files, every id must appear exactly once, and the pytest exit code must be consistent with the counts. Treat a run without a genuine session end (no `short test summary info` block / rc inconsistent with counts) as failed, not parse_error. In run_suite, when no summary parses never set passed=total; set passed=0 regardless of rc.

findings.description: The same `final` tree is bind-mounted :rw and reused across sequential suite runs: hidden tests (line 1080), then the regression command (1090), then for refactor tasks the structural check (1101). prepare() restores grader_protected paths and overlays hidden files only once, before the first run. Agent code executed during the first run (test import side effects) can rewrite the overlaid structural check, the regression tests, or the protected fixture files at their dest paths in /workspace so that the later runs grade a tampered tree.
findings.failure_mode: Agent-written code turns a red structural check or regression suite green by overwriting the grader's overlaid files between runs on the same tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run prepare() (or use a fresh copy of the tree) immediately before every run_suite call, or mount the tree read-only and give pytest a writable tmpfs for caches. Optionally hash the overlaid files after each run and flag any change as tampering in grade.json.

findings.description: Node ids and collection-error paths parsed from the agent-influenced pytest output are joined with os.path.join(tree, path) and opened with .read(). An absolute or `..` path discards the tree prefix, so an `ERROR /dev/zero` or `FAILED /dev/urandom::t` line makes the grader read an infinite device into memory (OOM), an `ERROR tests/fifo` naming a FIFO the agent created inside /workspace during the run blocks the grader forever, and any host file can be opened (a weak oracle: count of `def test` lines). The churn() reader (line 732) likewise reads every sandbox file fully with no size cap.
findings.failure_mode: The graded agent hangs or crashes the grader process (and the batch) by emitting a crafted node id; limited read oracle on host files.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate every output-derived path with safe_rel(), require it to resolve inside the tree, os.lstat() it and only open S_ISREG files below a size cap (e.g. 2 MiB); never open device nodes, FIFOs or symlinks. Apply the same cap to churn() and to the review/feedback markdown reads.

findings.description: remove_path walks a directory and calls os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700) for every entry in `dirs`. os.walk lists symlinks-to-directories in `dirs`, and os.chmod follows symlinks on Linux, so a symlink planted by the agent (copy_tree faithfully recreates sandbox symlinks into grading/final; extract_snapshot keeps in-tree symlinks) is dereferenced and its target is chmod'ed. This is reachable via put_file() → remove_path(dst) when a grader_protected directory collides with an agent directory containing `x -> /home/<grader>`, via fresh_dir(grading) on a re-grade of a run whose previous grading tree has such links, and via the finally-block remove_path(SCRATCH).
findings.failure_mode: The graded agent changes the mode of arbitrary directories owned by the grading user (home, ~/.ssh, shared data dirs) to 0700, breaking other processes or users.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip entries where os.path.islink(path) is true before chmod (or use os.chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False) where supported and fall back to skipping), and drop the chmod pass entirely in favour of shutil.rmtree(onerror=...) that chmods only after a failed unlink of a real directory.

findings.description: The docker run has --network none and --read-only but no --memory, --pids-limit, --cpus, --cap-drop or no-new-privileges. The inner `timeout 120` sends only SIGTERM (no -k), which a test process can ignore. When the outer subprocess timeout (180 s) fires, Python kills only the docker CLI client; the container is not named and is never killed, so with --rm it keeps running untouched.
findings.failure_mode: Agent code fork-bombs or allocates memory until the grading host is unusable, or leaves immortal containers behind after every grade; a single malicious run stalls the whole batch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `--memory 1g --memory-swap 1g --pids-limit 256 --cpus 2 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --name <uuid>`; use `timeout -k 10 120`; on TimeoutExpired run `docker kill <name>`. In host mode apply ulimit -u/-v via a wrapper or refuse (see AG-06).

findings.description: --executor host runs the agent-written tree's test command directly on the grading host as the invoking user. `env -i` only scrubs environment variables; the code still has the caller's filesystem (~/.aws, ~/.claude.json, ~/.ssh, the suite's hidden/ directories of every other task) and unrestricted network access. PYTHONUSERBASE additionally points at the caller's user site. The mode is opt-in but carries no guard or warning.
findings.failure_mode: A single graded agent exfiltrates grader credentials and the full hidden test suite, or persists on the host, defeating the DEC-0491 isolation goal.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate host mode behind an explicit `--unsafe-host` flag with a stderr warning, and run it under `unshare -n` / bwrap with only the tree, a scratch HOME and the interpreter visible; alternatively drop host mode for grading and keep it for self-check only.

findings.description: review.md, engineer-feedback.md and auditor-sprint-feedback.md are agent-authored and are read in full with no size limit, then fed to CITE.finditer. The path branch `[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}[`*)]{0,3}:` backtracks O(n) per start position on input such as `a.a.a.a…` with no colon, giving O(n²) overall; a few megabytes of such text keeps the grader busy for hours. gate_verdict/review_md_verdict also iterate unbounded files.
findings.failure_mode: The graded agent wedges the grader (and the batch) with a crafted review.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap each agent-authored text at a fixed size (e.g. 1 MiB, truncating and recording `truncated: true`), and tighten the path regex so the `+` class excludes `.` (match `(?:[^\s.]+\.)*[^\s.]+\.ext`), or pre-split on whitespace and apply the regex per token.

findings.description: grade.json is written through a predictable `<out>.tmp` path opened with plain open(..., 'w'), which follows a pre-existing symlink. In a host-mode pipeline run the agent can write outside sandbox/ (relative `../grade.json.tmp` is not caught by the contamination scan, which only looks at absolute Bash words) and leave a symlink there; the grader then truncates and overwrites the link target with the JSON before renaming the link over grade.json.
findings.failure_mode: Arbitrary file overwrite (with grade JSON contents) as the grading user, e.g. clobbering runs.jsonl or a dotfile.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the temp file with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=d, delete=False) or os.open(tmp, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW), and refuse if `out` itself is a symlink.

findings.description: In host mode the contamination scan allowlists the caller's ~/.aws, ~/.claude.json and ~/.codex, so an agent that reads AWS or API credentials by absolute path is never marked contaminated. The `hidden` substring check is also trivially bypassed (`hid""den`, globbing, `$(printf ...)`), and only absolute Bash words are considered, so `../../tasks/*/hidden` style traversal via relative paths is invisible. The header documents the scan as a lower bound, but grade consumers see `contaminated: null` as clean.
findings.failure_mode: Credential reads and hidden-suite access by the agent go unflagged; contamination statistics understate leakage.
findings.suggested_fix: Flag (not allowlist) ~/.aws and ~/.claude.json reads with a distinct pattern such as `credential_path`; add relative-path and glob heuristics for `hidden` and `..` traversal; emit a `scan_coverage: lower_bound` field so consumers do not treat null as proof of cleanliness.
